This book begins with an introduction in which Almustafa, the title character, prepares to return by ship to his native land after spending twelve years in the city of Orphalese, whose inhabitants have come to love and revere him. Before embarking, Almustafa's friend Almitra persuades him to talk of life, and twenty-six essays on various aspects of life follow. This is, a brief description of what 1923 novel, the most famous of Kahlil Gibran?

In later life he directed for television, wrote the novel _The Notebooks of Captain George_ and the play _Orvet_, and made such forgettable films as _Diary of a Chambermaid_ and _The Woman on the Beach_. He began making films in 1932 with _The Night at the Crossroards_, followed by such works as _The Human Beast_, _Madame Bovary_, and _The Rules of the Game_. For 10 points name this French director, also famous for _The Grand Illusion_.

Pts: This author published her first collection of stories, _The Troll Garden_, while a teacher. Its success led to her appointment as managing editor of McClure's magazine, which she left in 1912 to devote herself to novels, publishing _Alexander's Bridge_, her first, that year. 20 pts: Later works include _One of Ours_, for which she won a Pulitzer Prize, _Obscure Destinies_, and _Song of the Lark_. 10 pts: She is best known for such works as _O, Pioneers!_ and _My Antonia_.

His short stories are noted for their sardonic, biting tone and their aggressively negative characterization of the wealthy, including such works as the mock fable "Ants and the Grasshopper." Perhaps his best-known short story focuses on the thoughts rushing through the mind of a condemned spy in the moment before his execution by hanging. FTP, identify this author of "An Occurrance at Owl Creek Bridge."

Educated at the Jansenist school of Port-Royal, his first two tragedies, "La Thebaide" and "Alexandre le grande", were produced by Moliere. In 1677, he was appointed historiographer to Louis XIV, and thereafter only wrote two plays, "Esther" and "Athalie", both for the girls school of Saint-Cyr. FTP, name this French dramatist of "Bajazet", "Berenice", "Iphigenie en Aulide", and "Phedre".

This play's title character has his property confiscated after refusing to pay a tax to defend the island from the Turks. After his daughter Abigail seeks refuge in a nunnery, he poisons them all and strangles the friar who converted his daughter. He allies himself with the Turks and assists them in taking the city, but later meets a gruesome end by falling into a cauldron of boiling oil. FTP, name this play which centers around the merchant Barabas, written around 1589 by Christopher Marlowe.

A member of the Yiddish triumvirate, this Russian Jewish writer has been called "The Yiddish Mark Twain". He wrote stories popular all over the world, including The Adventures of Mottel, the Old Country, and Tevye's Daughter. FTP name this writer best remembered as the author of the basis for the musical "Fiddler on the Roof."

In 1835, his poem "Paracelsus" led him to an acquaintance with an actor, and he flirted with writing drama. His plays A Soul's Tragedy, Stafford, and Colombe's Birthday are all virtually forgotten, but his talents for characterization as in his DramaticPortraits are not. Name this Romantic Poet of Fra Lippo Lippi, Andrea del Satro, and My Last Duchess.

In this novel, the title character gets hosed as he accidentally kills a girl and fails to escape the authorities who aren't fooled by his false ransom note, and hose him off a rooftop. He then recruits a communist lawyer to defend him, and after losingthe case, is executed. Bigger Thomas is the title character of what work by Richard Wright?

Funk & Wagnalls Dictionary describes it as a motif of folk tales in which a hero comes upon an ill-treated corpse. After he gives his last penny to help fund a proper burial, the hero meets a traveling companion who aids him in some impossible task. The companion finally reveals himself to be the corpse that the hero helped. Outside folk tales, this monicker applies to: Bob Weir, Phil Lesh, Mickey Hart, Bill Kreutzmann, and formerly Jerry Garcia. FTP, give the name that the legend and people have in common.

Known as the French Shakespeare, and the Founder of French Tragedy, this rival of Moliere was criticized at the opening of his Le Cid because it did not conform to the three major unities. He went on to write more conventional works, however, including Horace and Cinna. FTP, name this French dramatist of the masterpiece Polyeucte.

Known primarily as a liberal humanist, this author was born only a year before his father was killed in World War I. He contributed to the theater by adapting Dostoyevsky's _Possessed_ and Faulkner's _Requiem for a Nun_ to the stage, although his plays never achieved the fame of his novels. Name this Algerian-born author whose most important works include _The Fall_, _The Plague_, and _The Stranger_.

It first appeared in 1837 and includes such stories as "Sights from a Steeple," "David Wan," "The Amibitious Guest," "A ril from the Town‑Pump," "The Seven Vagabonds," "Little Annie's Ramble," and "Dr. Heidegger's Experiment." FTP, identify this collection of short stories by Nathaniel Hawthorne.

This heroic poem centers on the exploits of Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nak ula, and Sahadeva, otherwise known as the Pandavas. The action focuses on the conflict between the Pandevas and their cousins, the Kauravas. Before the great war, Krishna sings the Bhagavad-Gita. Name this Hindu epic of the 5th century B.C.

An associate of James Joyce, he aided Joyce in the translation of a portion of his novel _Finnegans Wake_ into the French. This author's last published work was _Nacht and Traume_ and his first seperately published creative work was a poem entitled "Whoroscope." FTP, name this author of the novels _Murphy_, _Watt_, and _Molloy_ and the play _Endgame_.

When she is born it is prophesied that she will become the most beautiful woman of Ireland and that she will bring bloodshed and death. To avert the prophecy, Conchobar, king of Ulster, determines to marry her when she comes of age. She is raised by the nurse Lavarcham. Lavarcham's stories about Noisi, nephew of Conchobar, fire her imagination. They meet, fall in love and flee to Scotland. Upon return he is killed and she commits suicide. Name her for 10 points.

The last name's the same: Sterling, an influential African American critic who wrote _The Southern Road_; William Wells, the first known African- American to publish a novel, _Clotel_, in 1853; William, the author of _The Power of Sympathy_; Charles, who wrote the gothic novel _Wieland_; Dee, the author of _Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee_; Father, the fictional priest and detective in novels by GK Chesterton; and John, whose body is immortalized by Stephen Vincent Benet. FTP, give the literary name.

The title figure had "decided not to Live but Know" in this man's poem "A Grammarian's Funeral." The famous lines "God's in his heaven--/All's right with the world" come from his dramatic poem "Pippa Passes." His 12-book narrative of the murder trial of Guido Franceschini, based on an account he bought in a Florence booksellers' market, is titled The Ring and the Book. A young woman is described as having a "heart... Too soon made glad," leading the title noble to "give commands" so "all [her] smiles stopped together" in his best-known poem. FTP name this Victorian author of "My Last Duchess."

First published in The Crisis in 1921, a biographer of this poem's author relates that this poem was written in nearly final form on a train ride from Illinois to Missouri. The speaker describes his awareness of title entities "older than the flow of human blood in human veins," stating that he heard one "singing" when "Abe Lincoln/went down to New Orleans." Near another the speaker "built [his] hut," while near another he "raised the pyramids." Citing the Euphrates, Congo, Nile, and Mississippi, FTP what is this poem by Langston Hughes in which the speaker says his "soul has grown deep like" the title waterways?

One work by this composer tells the story of King Waldemar, who gives the titular castle to Tove, whose murder is detailed in the "Song of the Wood Dove." In addition to the cantata Gurre-Lieder, he composed a work that makes use of the Sprechstimme technique, and begins with the movement "Mondestrunken." In addition to composing the opera Moses and Aaron, the string sextet Transfigured Night and the song cycle Pierrot Lunaire, this man taught Anton von Webern and Alban Berg. FTP name this Austrian composer who developed the twelve-tone technique of composition.

After an introduction by the chorus of elders in this play, the former queen describes her dream of two women in fine dress yoked to a chariot; when one breaks her reins, the queen's son is tossed from the chariot and rends his cloak. Then a messenger arrives to tell Atossa that her son has survived a terrible naval defeat, leading her to visit the tomb of her husband, whose ghost rebukes his son for hubris, particularly in his futile attempt to build a bridge of ships across the Hellespont. Produced in 472 BCE with funding by Pericles, FTP what is this earliest extant work by Aeschylus which chronicles the defeat of the title invaders led by Xerxes?

A futuristic version of this American city was the home of Rick Deckard in Philip K. Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep. Dave Eggers moves himself and two siblings from Illinois to this city in his somewhat exaggerated memoir, A Heartbreaking Work of Staggering Genius. This city's namesake "Renaissance" included the poets Lew Welch and Philip Whalen, with author/teacher Kenneth Rexroth at the forefront. Those poets were joined by Gary Snyder at the famous 1956 reading at the Six Gallery in this city, at which Allan Ginsberg's "Howl" was first read. Also the setting of The Maltese Falcon and Lawrence Ferlinghetti's City Lights bookstore is, FTP, what California city featured in Randy Shilts's The Mayor of Castro Street, a biography of Harvey Milk, and Vikram Seth's The Golden Gate?

In an early poem by this author, the persona states that "The force that through the green fuse drives the flower/Drives my green age." Another poem concludes, "After the first death, there is no other." Along with "A Refusal to Mourn the Death, by Fire, of a Child in London," he also wrote a radio play, Under Milk Wood, and an autobiography, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Dog. His best known work is a villanelle addressed to the speaker's father arguing that "Old age should burn and rave at close of day." FTP name this Welsh author of "Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night."

In its final form, this collection included a description of the narrator's tour of Westminster Abbey and a Gothic tale of a cavalier, Herman von Starkenfaust, who pretends to be a goblin to wed the daughter of a baron. The stories are connected by the titular gentleman-narrator, whose visits with the Bracebridge family were eventually incorporated into this work. Its two most famous parts claim to have been told to the narrator by a New York Dutchman, one describing the contest for Katrina between Brom Bones and Ichabod Crane, and the other the 20-year sleep of a Patroon. FTP what is this collection, including "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" and "Rip Van Winkle," written by Washington Irving?

In one literary work, a giant one of these animals enlists the collections officer Katagiri to help battle Worm and prevent an earthquake. That creature is a "Super" type that "Saves Tokyo" in a story by Haruki Murakami. This animal is the namesake of a comedy in which Xanthias is forced to wear Heracles' lion skin, and Dionysus brings back Aeschylus from Hades. In addition to naming that work by Aristophanes, this type of animal is owned by the gambler Jim Smiley, but has lead pellets poured down its throat to prevent it from being "celebrated" for its "jumping" in "Calaveras County." name this type of amphibian found in a Mark Twain story.

In one scene in this novel, Agustín punches one character in the face several times and calls him a "horse lover" in an attempt to provoke him into a fight. After that character, Pablo, goes out to check on his horses, a group including the main character and Pilar plan to kill him. Pablo later steals dynamite from the main character, who reflects angrily on the theft while lying in bed next to Maria. However, Pablo returns later with the dynamite, which allows the main character to proceed successfully with his plot to blow up a bridge. Robert Jordan breaks his leg and awaits death at the hands of Fascists at the end of, FTP, what Hemingway novel with a title taken from John Donne?

On the first day of the main character's trip in this novel, he stays in a guesthouse in Salisbury and remembers an incident in which his father drove around two drunken houseguests with the greatest of courtesy until they started insulting his employer, at which point his father pulled over the car until they apologized. In this novel, the main character's new employer, Mr. Farraday, makes him take a weeklong road trip vacation through England. The main character sets out to find Miss Kenton, the former housekeeper of Darlington Hall, in an attempt to bring her back to the house. The butler Stevens narrates what novel by Kazuo Ishiguro?

This author is credited with the origins of the "Second Wave" of the movement she is associated with. Her most famous work addresses the "problem with no name" and came about as a result of surveying her Smith College classmates. She went on to found the National Organization for Women after publishing a book suggesting that the modern world forces women to define themselves through their husbands and children. Name this feminist author of The Feminine Mystique.

This work's basso ostinato has been parodied in works by Handel and Mozart. Originally written for three violins and a basso continuo, it has since been arranged for various ensembles, although few modern performances include the gigue [zheeg] that originally accompanied the piece. An eight note sequence in the bass repeats 28 times in this work frequently performed at weddings, the most famous piece of music by Johann Pachelbel.

One author from this country wrote about a naïve village boy recruited to fight in a civil war in his "novel in rotten English," Sozaboy. Another author from this country was awarded the 1991 Booker Prize for his best known work, The Famished Road. Another novel by an author from this nation is No Longer at Ease, which recounts the firing of a government worker, Obi Okonkwo, whose similarly named grandfather was the protagonist of the novel Things Fall Apart. Name this nation of Ken Saro-Wiwa, Ben Okri and Chinua Achebe.

Theophrastus wrote that this author's one completed work was a papyrus he left in the Temple of Artemis which criticized Anaximander for underestimating the role of injustice in men's lives. Diogenes Laertius wrote that his works were left unfinished because of melancholia, which caused him to be referred to as the "the weeping philosopher." His is known for arguing that "everything is in a state of flux," and he established a term for the fundamental order of the cosmos: Logos. Name this pre-Socratic thinker who thought all matter was made of fire and said something about not being able to step into the same river twice.

This author's first book was a somewhat dismissive biography of a Pre- Raphaelite writer titled Rossetti: His Life and Works. He described the dismissal of Paul Pennyfeather from Oxford in his first novel, Decline and Fall, while William Boot gets the title sensational story in his novel Scoop. Another novel of his focuses on the marriage breakdown of Tony and Lady Brenda Last, and in his most well-known novel Charles Ryder tells the story of the Marchmain family. Name this author of A Handful of Dust and Brideshead Revisited.

In one very short story by this author, Mrs. Mallard is secretly pleased by news of her husband Brently's death, but she has a heart attack when she learns that he actually survived a train crash. Another short work sees Calixta cheat on her husband with Alcee during the title event, a story so controversial it was only published in 1969, 70 years after composition. Besides "The Story of an Hour" and "The Storm," this author most famously wrote of another affair, this one leading to the suicide of the protagonist when she drowns herself. Describing the illicit romance of Robert LeBrun and Edna Pontellier, FTP name this author of The Awakening.

This author satirized the Calvinism of Jonathan Edwards in a poem about a "Deacon's Masterpiece" that lasted exactly 100 years and then fell apart all at once, "The Wonderful One-Hoss Shay." One of the so-called Fireside Poets, a speaker in one of his poems exhorts, "Build thee more stately mansions, O my soul," while another begins with a call to "tear [the] tattered ensign down" from the title vessel, which was being retired. Also the author of the series of essays titled The Autocrat of the Breakfast Table, FTP name this poet of "The Chambered Nautilus" and "Old Ironsides," father and namesake of a Supreme Court justice.

This man used the word "amative" to describe the love of man for woman and the word "adhesive" to describe the love of man for man; the former type dominates his cycle of poems called "Children of Adam," while the latter dominates his "Calamus" cycle. He describes becoming "tired and sick" during the title time and later looking up "in perfect silence at the stars" in his "When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer," while in another poem he describes the "Flood-tide below me!" in "Crossing Brooklyn Ferry." FTP name this American author who included these works, as well as the massive "Song of Myself," in his ever-growing collection Leaves of Grass.

This figure was admonished, "O come, you pious youth; adore / The wisdom of thy God" in a poem to her by Jupiter Hammon. This poet argues, "'Tis Satan's snares a-fluttering in the wind / Whereby he has ensnared thy foolish mind" in her "Deism", a lost work published in 1977 in the New England Quarterly. The Christianity she was taught informed much more of her poetry, including "Goliath of Gath", but she also penned an ode to Neptune on a mistress's voyage to England. Thomas Jefferson panned her compositions as "beneath the dignity of criticism," and Henry Louis Gates has written on the Trials of, what author of Poems on Various Subjects, Religious and Moral, a Boston slave and founding figure in African-American literature?

A magazine editor claims that his pet baboon, Juniper, has written Gothic tales for a certain magazine in this author's short story "How to Write a Blackwood Article." In the best-selling work of his lifetime a Black man named Jupiter describes a map of the location of Captain Kidd's treasure to William Legrand. In addition to "The Gold Bug," this author wrote of the twins Madeline and Roderick whose home collapses into a bog in a story collected in Tales of the Grotesque and Arabesque. FTP name this American creator of the detective C. Auguste Dupin who also wrote "The Fall of the House of Usher."

A fictional version of this man claims that women are coming to kill him at a festival at the opening of Aristophanes' play Thesmophoriazusae. This illustrates Aristophanes' view that works by this man like Philoctetes and Ion portrayed women badly. One of his best-known works ends with the title figure appearing above the stage in the chariot of Helios, bearing the bodies of her children, whom she killed herself, away from her husband who left her for Glauce. FTP name this author of Medea and The Trojan Women.

Mary Catherine Bateson, the daughter of the author of this book, wrote a new forward for it, "Words for a New Century," which discusses the theme of the last chapter, "Education for Choice." It was heavily criticized in a work subtitled "The Making and Unmaking of an Anthropological Myth," written by Derek Freeman. Its thesis suggests that children and teenagers in the titular society suffer less psychologically due to looser sexual mores than teenagers in America. FTP name this controversial anthropological study written by Margaret Mead.

Carl Sandburg describes buying some brass knuckles in this historical figure's "city" in his poem "Knucks." Vachel Lindsay described this man "pacing up and down... Near the old court house" in his poem with a title stating that this man "walks at midnight," while Edwin Arlington Robinson called him "The Master" in another poem. His best known poetic chronicler described him in "This Dust Was Once the Man" as well as in a poem in which he apostrophizes him as "the fallen Western star," the poem "When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom'd." FTP who is this historical figure whom Walt Whitman also apostrophized as "O Captain! My Captain!"?

The word "vegetable" is used in an archaic manner to mean "flourishing" in this poem, describing the speaker's love that could "grow/Vaster than empires." The speaker urges his addressee to "roll all our strength and all/Our sweetness up into one ball" and states that, "though we cannot make our sun/Stand still, yet we can make him run." The speaker argues that the addressee's "quaint honor [will] turn to dust" soon enough, so they should "sport us while we may." Suggesting the title behavior would be "no crime" had they "but world enough and time," FTP what is this poem in which the speaker tries to convince a woman to get with him, the most famous work of Andrew Marvell?

This man published his first two works, the plays Henry III and his Court and Christine, while working for the Duc d'Orleans, whose ascension to the throne as Louis Philippe this man supported. His novel, George, deals with issues of colonialism and race and was largely inspired by the experiences of his parternal grandmother, a French-African Haitian. Another novel, The Vicomte de Bragelonne, is divided into three parts, the last of which is The Man in the Iron Mask. For 10 points name this author who created the character of Edmond Dantes in The Count of Monte Cristo.

The author was going to name the main character of this book Connie Gustafson, but changed it to one that better fit her personality. That girl, a 19 year old from Texas who has just moved to New York City, has numerous, rich lovers, including Rusty Trawler. On Thursdays she gets the "weather report" from Sally Tomato who is being held at Sing Sing prison. She dubs the unnamed narrator "Fred" and they become friends. Only the title location can cure Holly Golightly of the "mean reds" in, what Truman Capote novel that inspired a movie featuring George Peppard and Audrey Hepburn?

Ganya asks this character if he would marry such a woman as the one in a portrait in General Epanchin's office at the beginning of the novel in which this character appears. This man replies, "I can't marry anybody, I'm unwell." Dr. Schneider treats his illness somewhat successfully in Switzerland, although he still occasionally has seizures. At a party, this character witnesses the woman with whom he is in love throw a hundred thousand rubles, given to her by Rogozhin, into a fireplace. That woman, Nastasya Filipovna, eventually discloses that she loves the main character, but fears that she would destroy him if they were together. Identify this title character of a Dostoevsky novel.

This author described the dissolution of the marriage of Marcia and Bartley Hubbard in one novel, while in another the Socialist Civil War veteran Lindau is contends with the millionaire Dryfoos as observed by the narrator, Basil March. In addition to A Modern Instance and A Hazard of New Fortunes, this man served as editor of The Atlantic Monthly in the 1870s. His best-known novel details the title character's attempts to buy his way into the upper- class by marrying his daughter to Tom Corey after making his fortune in the paint business. Name this author of The Rise of Silas Lapham.

The speaker cries out that he will "fly to" the title figure in this poem, "Not charioted by Bacchus and his pards,/But on the viewless wings of Poesy." Later he addresses the title figure as "Darkling," and admits that he has "been half in love with easeful Death." The poem ends with an illustration of the author's concept of "negative capability," with the speaker wondering about the title figure's song, "Was it a vision, or a waking dream? Fled is that music—do I wake or sleep?" FTP what is this 1819 poem which begins, "My heart aches, and a drowsy numbness pains/My sense," a work addressed to an avian creature by John Keats?

This language "in America" is the subtitle of the short story "Envy," describing the title feeling of Edelshtein for Ostrover in a work by Cynthia Ozick. Practitioner Mendele Sforim's works were translated from this language into Russian by Isaac Babel, while humorist Leo Rosten wrote a work about "The Joys of" this language. Enemies, a Love Story and The Spinoza of Market Street are works in this language by Isaac Bashevis Singer, while another popular story written in this language is "Tevye The Milkman," which provided the basis for the musical "Fiddler on the Roof." FTP what is this language written in by Sholem Aleichem?

This man described a "moon [that] rattles like a fragment of angry candy" in a poem about "[t]he Cambridge ladies who live in furnished souls." The title figure of another poem was "more brave than me: more blond than you" and avers that "there is some shit [he] will not eat"; that poem is "i sing of Olaf glad and big." Another work depicts the title creature "gathering to leap" in an arrangement of diagonal letters that can be seen as a concrete image of the rearranged letters of "grasshopper." Also having written of the "goat-footed balloonman" in the poem "in just spring," FTP name this author of "my father moved through dooms of love" who is known for his lack of capitalization.

This author popularized the idea of seeing pink elephants as a symbol of drunkenness in an autobiographical novel detailing his own problems with drink called John Barleycorn. His socialist outlook is evident in the novels The Cruise of the Snark and his tale of the eventual overthrow of the fascist Oligarchy by the Brotherhood of Man, titled The Iron Heel. He's best known for one novel in which Kiche's offspring is eventually domesticated, and another in which the dog Buck eventually accedes to the title urge. FTP name this author of the Yukon-set novels White Fang and The Call of the Wild.

The contemporary Peruvian novelist Mario Vargas Llosa devoted his book, The Perpetual Orgy, to this 19th century writer. One of this author's short stories is about a poor peasant girl who at the moment of her death sees her beloved pet parrot as the Holy Spirit waiting for her in heaven. That story, "A Simple Heart" along with "The Legend of St. Julian the Hospitalier " and "Herodias" make up this Frenchman's Trois Contes, or Three Stories. Other works of his include the posthumously published Bouvard et Pecuchet and a historical novel about Carthage, Salammbo. FTP name this influential Realist writer of A Sentimental Education and Madame Bovary.

This author examined French, and more generally, human complicity in the Holocaust in 1964's Incident at Vichy. The lives of Italian-American dockworkers and the eventual stabbing of Eddie Carbone is the subject of this author's 1955 work A View from the Bridge. The protagonist of another play, Joe Keller, kills himself at the end after revelations that he was aware he sold faulty parts to the US Air Force, leading to the deaths of 21 pilots, in this man's All My Sons. FTP identify this American playwright best known for creating Biff and Happy, the sons of Willy Loman, in Death of a Salesman.

When this character is first seen in a chapter named for him, the narrator notes the white scar on his left cheek that looks "like lightning," leading the narrator to note that this character has a "crucifixion on his face." Soon after, Stubb tells Flask that he had a dream of being kicked by this man, and in the dream a merman told him this is an honor. The leader of this man's "five dusky phantoms," Fedallah, prophecies that he will see two hearses before he dies, and that only hemp can kill him, a prophecy which comes true when he is dragged into the ocean tied by a harpoon rope to his nemesis. FTP name this captain of the Pequod whose leg and life were taken by Moby Dick.

Two unfinished sections of this work are known as the "Cantos of Mutabilitie." In this work's Book Five, the personification of the "calumnious voice" of the world, the "Blatant Beast," is captured by Calidore, the personification of courtesy, but it later breaks free. Earlier, Grantorto's plan to kill Irena, the personification of Ireland, is thwarted when he's beheaded by Talus, the friend of Arthegall. Book I focuses primarily on Una's salvation of her lover from the threats of lust. FTP what is this allegory in which the Red Crosse Knight represents holiness and Glorianna is the title monarch, the best-known work of Edmund Spenser?

This artist's one published novel is the 1965 experimental work Tarantula, and Christopher Ricks, noted expert on John Milton, published an analysis of this man's writings called "Visions of Sin." He has recently released his first holiday album, Christmas in the Heart, with proceeds going to charity. His brief electric set at the Newport Folk Festival in 1965 caused controversy with folk purists, coming hard on his release of the album Bringing It All Back Home which included the song "Maggie's Farm." FTP who is this singer-songwriter of "Mr. Tambourine Man" and "Like a Rolling Stone"?

The characters of Captain Keeney and Smitty both appear in this man's works Ile and The Moon of the Caribees. Driscoll's climactic, agonizing death is incommensurable with the routine of shipping life in this author's Bound East for Cardiff. The character Con Melody is a braggart in this man's More Stately Mansions and its predecessor, A Touch of the Poet, while the stoker Yank despairingly dies in the rough embrace of a gorilla in this man's The Hairy Ape. Perhaps better known for his work about Hickey's attempts to shatter the dreams of the drinkers of Harry Hope's saloon, FTP name this author of The Iceman Cometh and Long Day's Journey into Night.

When this character's daughter Pammy was born, she "wept uncontrollably" for an hour because she had a girl instead of a boy, later expressing the hope that Pammy will become a "beautiful little fool." She teases her husband for trying to push the book The Rise of Colored Empires on her second cousin, who narrates the work in which she appears. Described as having a voice "full of money," she takes no responsibility for running down Myrtle Wilson. Symbolized by a green light on her dock to the protagonist, FTP who is this wife of Tom Buchanan and love interest of Jay Gatsby?

This author decried modern attitudes toward the elderly in the 1972 work La Viellese, translated as The Coming of Age. This author also wrote The Ethics of Ambiguity and was a signatory of the "Manifesto of 343," which bore the signatures of women who publicly admitted having had illegal abortions. Her best-known work examined the title people in literature and history and stated that putting a woman on a pedestal allows man to keep her in a pit. Author of the novel The Mandarins and a one-time lover of Nelson Algren, FTP name this author of The Second Sex who also wrote Adieux: Farewell to Sartre.

This author wrote a short story in which the coal miner Walter Bates dies in a cave-in, and Elizabeth associates the smell of the title plants with death. In addition to "Odour of Chrysanthemums," this author wrote a novel that features three generations of the Brangwen family, The Rainbow, as well as a novel in which Clara Dawes is rejected by Paul Morel. His best-known work is set at Wragby, and features the gamekeeper Mellors, who has an affair with Connie. Name this author of Sons and Lovers and Lady Chatterley's Lover.

This group's historical texts include the Tolidah and The Chronicle of Joshua, and this group rejects the authority of the Mishnah and Gemara. This group holds that Isaac was bound by Abraham on Mount Gerizim, making this place their spiritual center of worship. In John, a member of this group is asked to bring Jesus water from Jacob's Well, and a parable related in the Gospel of Luke about a man who traveled to Jericho and was attacked by bandits tells of a member of this group who assisted him. FTP name this people whose enmity for the Jews explains Jesus's use of the example of a "good" one to illustrate the need to help a neighbor in need.

Ferapont tries to exorcise the room of a recently deceased holy man in this work, partly because that man's corpse had defied the hopes of the monks and exuded a putrid stench immediately upon his death, unsettling the faith of one of the title figures. That character later has a dream of the deceased priest visiting with him at the Wedding Feast of Cana, at which Father Zossima tells him he has redeemed the peasant girl Grushenka, who had earlier slept with his sibling. That sibling stands trial for the murder of their father, Fyodor, who was actually killed by his bastard son Smerdyakov. Ending with Dmitri's exile to Siberia and a statement of Alyosha's faith, FTP name this novel by Fyodor Dostoevsky.

The site described in this poem is "twice five miles of fertile ground/With walls and towers... Girdled round" and is filled with "incense- bearing tree[s]." The speaker describes seeing "an Abyssinian Maid" sing of Mount Abora. One who travels there would see its "caves of ice" and feed on its "honey-dew" and "milk of paradise." Located where "Alph, the sacred river, ran" and home to a "stately pleasure dome," FTP Xanadu is the home of what title ruler in a poem by Samuel Taylor Coleridge?

Herbert M. Hoxie was the only bidder for work this entity was incorporated to undertake and hence in name received the contract. Moxie turned the contract over to Thomas Durant, who ensured that the company's liability to investors would extend only as far as their investment, not their personal wealth, a first in US history. The company paid itself to provide construction materials, starting work by adding a useless nine-mile oxbow to its first track section to increase profits. The scandal was uncovered in letters sent to Henry McComb by the man who ousted Durant from the company's board, letters implicating Henry Wilson and Schuyler Colfax. FTP what was this finance and construction company created to supply the Union and Central Pacific Railroads, most famously led by congressman Oakes Ames?

The useless slaughter of thousands of migrating pigeons by Richard Jones contrasts his greed and waste with the shooting of just one pigeon for food by this character. Later, as sheriff of Templeton, Jones arrests this character for assaulting Hiram Doolittle and for burning his own shack rather than allowing a warrant to be presented to enter it on the pretext of searching for an illegally shot deer. This character flees to the west at the end of the novel, leading to his appearance in a subsequent book in which he is only known as "the trapper." The Pioneers and The Prairie are chronologically the last two books to chronicle the life of, FTP, what protagonist whose earlier life was described in The Pathfinder, The Deerslayer, and The Last of the Mohicans?

This is the language of the novel in which Bras Cubas narrates episodic events from his life after his death, Epitaph of a Small Winner. This is the language of a novel in which Nacib Saad's romance with the title woman shocks the local macho culture, as well as one in which Vandinho dies while dancing but comes back as a ghost to live with his wife. Those two works, Gabriela, Clove and Cinnamon and Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands are by Jorge Amado. The Stone Raft was written in this language, as was another work by the same author in which the title affliction affects all the central characters but a doctor's wife, who helps them survive a hellish time in a prison, Blindness. FTP what is this language written in by Joachim Machado de Assis and Jose Saramago?

The horse trader Pat Stamper tricked one of these characters into trading for two worn-out mules in the story "Fool about a Horse," later incorporated into a novel about them. That same character purposely rubbed cow manure into the white rug of Major de Spain, whose insistence on reparations leads that character to commit arson on the Major's barn. That character's son marries Eula Varner and takes over the Jefferson bank from Manfred de Spain, though he is eventually killed by his cousin Mink at the end of The Mansion, the last novel in the trilogy named for this family. Including Ab, Sarty, and Flem, what is this family of hardscrabble characters in the works of William Faulkner?

One of this man's studies opens each chapter with an excerpt from a song, including "Children, You'll Be Called On" and "I'm A Rolling." One of his works was an analysis of an African-American community titled The Philadelphia Negro. In one work, he stated "The problem of the 20th Century is the Problem of the Color Line," and he resigned from editing The Crisis due to his increased Marxism. This man developed the idea that Black Americans should work to promote their top 10 percent, what he called the "Talented Tenth," and he openly opposed the accommodationist ethic Booker Washington. FTP name this founder of the NAACP who wrote The Souls of Black Folk.

The protagonist of this episode was the cousin of his opposition, but family ties did not stop him from forming a makeshift army and attacking the Doeg and Pamunkey tribes, in direct opposition to the orders of his kinsman. He also issued the Declaration of the People of Virginia. This laundry list of complaints against the government was a mild annoyance compared to the burning of Jamestown, which governor William Berkeley had only recently recaptured from the proclaimed traitors. FTP, what 1676 rebellion failed only after the sudden death of its namesake leader?

One poem by this author states "the Church is cold / But the Alehouse is healthy, and pleasant, and warm." In addition to writing "The Little Vagabond," this poet described "A little black thing among the snow / Crying 'weep weep' in notes of woe." Another poem by this author asks "What immortal hand or eye / Could frame thy fearful symmetry?" and describes the titular animal as "burning bright / In the forests of the night." Those poems by this author are collected in Songs of Innocence and Songs of Experiece. Name this English poet of "The Chimney Sweeper" and "The Tyger."

In one long poem by this author, the title man is "out of key with his time," striving to "resuscitate the dead art/Of poetry." Those lines open this man's "Hugh Selwyn Mauberly," while a much longer work of his includes sections titled "Leopoldine," "Rock-Drill" and "Throne," the last of which includes poems written while this author was incarcerated at St. Elizabeth's, a hospital to which he was sentenced when found incompetent to stand trial for treason for making WWII radio broadcasts in favor of Mussolini. Also famous for his open translations of Chinese poems, FTP name this poet of "The River- Merchant's Wife" and The Cantos who also edited Eliot's "The Waste-Land."

The Idler and The Rambler were two periodicals written by this man, and he popularized the term "Metaphysical Poets" in his series of biographies Lives of the Poets. The title prince travels with his mentor Imlac out of Happy Valley in search of true happiness in this author's prose work, Rasselas, while his greatest accomplishment was an epic of over 115,000 entries, the standard of its type until the creation of the Oxford English version. Author of an 18th-century Dictionary of the English Language, FTP name this British writer whose own biography was written by his one-time companion James Boswell.

The unnamed title female is brought to the title locale by Jack Potter after getting married in San Antonio in one of this author's stories; when Potter is confronted by Scratchy Wilson wanting a gunfight, he walks away flabbergasted at news that Potter has wed. In addition to "The Bride Comes to Yellow Sky," he described the oiler, the cook, the captain, and the correspondent surviving a boat's capsizing and eventually coming ashore near New Smyrna, Florida in another story. Another famous story depicts a fight between Johnny and the Swede at the title inn, leading the Swede to wander off to another fight in which he is stabbed to death. FTP name this author of the stories "The Open Boat" and "The Blue Hotel" as well as the novel The Red Badge of Courage.

The first work written after this author's so-called "inferno period" of mental instability was a trilogy called To Damascus, a failure at the box office. In a better-known work, the student Arkenholz befriends Hummel, an old man who commits suicide after his attempts to reveal the secrets of the residents of a boarding house shows him to be a monster. An earlier play shows the title character flirt and finally sleep with the manservant Jean, leading her to suicide with a razor. Also the author of A Dream Play and The Dance of Death, FTP who was this Swedish author of The Ghost Sonata and Miss Julie?

The title of this writer's novel Pinball, 1973 was a play on a title by Kenzaburo Oe and it introduced J, a bar owner who also appeared in A Wild Sheep Chase and Dance, Dance, Dance. He was himself the owner of a jazz bar called "Peter Cat," but the most important character in his early novels was called Rat. In the 1980's, he wrote Hard-Boiled Wonderland and the End of the World and Norwegian Wood, but he is more famous for a novel about a lazy man named Toru Okada whose cat disappears. Identify this Japanese author of Kafka on the Shore and The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle.

This person objected to a portrayal of him as Claude Lantier in the novel L'Ouevre, which caused him to break with Zola. Early works like 1867's The Abduction focus on haunting themes, but he soon took up Romanticism, as evidenced by Young Girl at the Piano - Overture to Tannhäuser. This artist turned to Impressionism in the 1870's with a series of views of his home at Jas de Bouffan. His later paintings were so deliberate that Still Life with Apples and Still Life with Plate of Cherries that depict waxed fruit. Identify this French Post-Impressionist painter best known for a series of views of Mont St. Victoire.

In a Bowdlerized version of this work, actions that occurred on "days when the rains came / Down in the hollow" are repeated in the narrator's memory "Behind the stadium." Released against its artist's wishes on Blowin' Your Mind!, this song's third verse notes that the title character was spotted "just the other day," after which the narrator remarks how much she has grown and notes that he is sometimes "overcome thinkin' ‘bout" previous experiences with her, namely, "Makin' love in the green grass" in the uncensored version. Identify this song by Van Morrison about a young lady with a certain feature.

This work's second part opens with the line "O sovereign power of love! O grief! O balm!" before the title character meets up with Venus and Adonis. It opens when the title character's sister Peona takes him away from a celebration of Pan. This poem's poet chose to use Cynthia instead of a more common name for its protagonist's love interest. Beginning with the line "A thing of beauty is a joy forever" and written when its author was just 21, identify this poem about a shepherd who falls for the moon goddess Selene written by John Keats.

This book uses the setting of an area built by fur traders for its protagonist to accept a man's proposal and sees pictures of his hometown. After they are married, this novel's central couple argues when she asks him whether he is jealous of the other doctors, but he eventually agrees to give her a checking account. A climax when that wife defends Fern Mullins against accusations that she corrupted the town's youth at a barn dance and soon after the wife leaves the town, realizing that she it or her husband. Set in Gopher Prairie, Minnesota is, what novel about Carol Kennicott written by Sinclair Lewis?

He wrote about Mr. Popo, a do-nothing carpenter; B. Wordsworth, a perfectionist poet; and Man-Man, a lunatic-turned-prophet in describing the events on a title street. His nonfiction works include Among the Believers, and he described the trip of a gay government official named Bobby in a fictional African country in the Booker-winning In a Free State. Perhaps best known is his tale of a man who marries into the Tulsi family and dreams of owning his own home. Name this author of A House for Mr. Biswas, a native of Trinidad.

This poem uses the metaphor of a laurel, which grows early but "withers quicker than the rose." The title figure of this poem becomes a "Townsman of a stiller town" when he is set down at his threshold. That title figure is called smart to "slip betimes away / from fields where glory does not stay." The speaker recalls when the title person was carried home shoulder-high after he won his town the race, and he dies while he still defends the championship trophy. For 10 points—name this elegy on the death of a youthful runner, a poem by A.E. Housman.

This poem's epigraphs allude to Joseph Conrad's Heart of Darkness and to the tradition of burning Guy Fawkes in effigy. It includes a children's rhyme about a prickly pear, and notes that the title figures have their "headpieces filled with straw", and that their "dry voices" are "quiet and meaningless." name this poem also about "the stuffed men" by T.S. Eliot, which asserts that the world ends "not with a bang but a whimper".

A major point of this novel is its questioning of freedom, as the characters only seem to understand love upon separation from each other. The character Cottard constantly fears arrest and punishment, while Tarrou's calm atheism contrasts with the fire and brimstone words of Father Paneloux, at whom the protagonist screams upon witnessing the death of a young boy. Opening with the death of the concierge at Dr. Rieux's building, name this novel about humanity's reaction to widespread disease and hopelessness, written by Albert Camus

This literary character is the intended recipient of a record called "Little Shirley Beans." A sibling doesn't vocalize his concerns that she will fail to grasp a brass ring, saying, "If they fall off, they fall off, but it's bad if you say anything to them," and also finds to protect her childlike innocence, in fact wondering what this character would think if she saw ‘fuck you' written on a museum wall. She realizes how much her older brother needs her maturity, and eventually corrects him, saying, "It's ‘If a body meet a body coming through the rye'!" name this ten-year-old sister of Holden Caulfield.

This character hosts an extravagant wedding at the Port Authority Bus Terminal in the second novel in which he appears. The one business deal that he lost money on was the purchase of Egyptian cotton as his attempts to turn this into food by covering it in chocolate failed. He justifies his actions, including having the Germans bomb Pianosa with the quote "What's Good for M&M industries is good for America." name this mess hall officer and black-market businessman from Catch-22 evidently named for his twisted logic.

This work's protagonist is based on Elena Stahov from Turgenev's On the Eve. In this novel, a failure to sell a horse leaves Caleb Garth in the lurch for a debt not covered by the expected Featherstone fortune. The vote for a new hospital chaplain is rigged in favor of Tyke by Nicholas Bulstrode, who is later blackmailed by Raffles. The protagonist's sister Celia dislikes men with moles and marries James Chettam, while the protagonist moves out of Tipton Grange and eventually achieves happiness with Will Ladislaw. The death of Edward Causabon widows Dorothea Brooke in what novel by George Eliot?
Middlemarch: A Study of Provincial Life

In one play by this author, a man falsely eavesdrops on a phone call to a lesbian Nazi before failing to imitate an affair with Jeanette Fisher. In addition to that play about Barney Cashman, he wrote about the Bratters moving into a new apartment and Eugene Jerome growing up in Depression Brooklyn. This author of Last of the Red Hot Lovers, Brighton Beach Memoirs, and Barefoot in the Park also described a man who moves in with the Pigeon sisters after helping his roommate with child support payments and hygiene. Name this writer who described Oscar Madison and Felix Ungar in The Odd Couple.

The protagonist of this novel keeps an x-ray of the skeleton of his crush on his dresser and eventually befriends Mynheer Peeperkorn. After learning about "the bad Russian table," that man meets a Jewish Jesuit, Naptha, who discusses philosophy with Settembrini. Despite consummation of the relationship during Carnival, World War I interrupts the romance of Clavdia Cauchat and the main character, who had come to visit his cousin Joachim Zemssen at the International Sanatorium Berghof. Name this novel about Hans Castorp by Thomas Mann.

This author twice used "Dark House" as a working title; its first use for a short story he eventually re-titled "Wash" and published alongside such stories as "Fox Hunt," "Barn Burning." and "Dry September." He also used "Dark House" for a novel featuring Lena Grove and Joe Christmas and eventually published as Light in August. Identify this Nobel Prize- winning Southern author known for such famous novels as Absalom, Absalom!, As I Lay Dying, and The Sound and the Fury.

Minor characters in this work include Flora Bervoix, the Marchese d'Obigny, and the Commissionario. The libretto for it was adapted from Dumas' "The Lady of the Camellias." Arias in this opera include "Di Madride noi siam mattadori," sung by Gastone and the bullfighters, and one beginning Act III shared by the soprano Annina and the opera's main character, a courtesan. Giorgio and Alfredo Germont pursue the titular "fallen woman," Violetta Valery. Identify this opera by Giussepe Verdi.

The matriarch of this work's central family initially refuses to bear her husband's children, worried they will have pig's tails. That woman is Ursula Iguaran, whose husband Jose Arcadio founds a new village, and the span of her lifetime provides one meaning for this novel's title. Name this novel about the founding of Macondo and the Buendia family, a work of in Gabriel Garcia Márquez.

Early devoting himsed to be "Chateaubriand or nothing," this writer's poetry includes the volues Autumn Leaves and Sunlight and Shadows, which followed his breakout, Odes and Ballads. Responsible for such plays as the unstagable Cromwell; Lucrecia Borgia; Marie Tudor; and Angelo, Tyrant of Padua, this author fled his country after 1851 took power, dedicating Toilers of the Sea to his adoptive home of Guernsey. This author won entry into the Cénacle with his early novel Hans of Iceland. Name this French Romantic author notable for Les Misérables.

G.K. Chesterton wrote a 1911 poem about this battle. Shortly before it began, the illegitimate son of Charles V ordered the forces split into four divisions in order to create a powerful central force. This battle saw the wounding and capture of Miguel de Cervantes. The final naval battle in world history solely between rowing vessels, it took place largely in the Gulf of Patras, and resulted in the flight of Ali Pasha's fleet and victory for Don John of Austria. Name this 1571 naval battle in which the Holy League crushed the Ottoman Empire.

One part of this long work was published as Albertine disparue to disambiguate it from a Tagore work, and some parts of it can be found in the author's previous Jean Santeuil. Its other portions include Sodom and Gomorrah and Time Regained. The narrator's love for Odette de Crecy plays a major role in its first part, and the presence of madeleines results in a critical realization in this work which was rejected by many publishers. Name this long series of novels including Swann's Way, written by Marcel Proust.

This work's narrator of this gains the nickname "Handel" from his friend Herbert and eventually helps him get a job with Wemmick; he also forms a great friendship in his youth with his brother-in-law Joe, a blacksmith. While at Satis House, the protagonist obsesses over Estella, whom he met at the home of Miss Havisham. Name this novel about the exploits of Phillip Pirrip, an 1861 work by Charles Dickens.

At one point in this play, a man and woman compare their lives for several minutes before realizing that their lives are identical as they are, in fact, married to one another. Another character arrives to ask politely if there are any fires in the household and, finding none, stays to exchange parables. After the arrival of the Fire Chief and the Martins, Mr. Smith gives his opinion that a conscientious doctor must die with his patient if unable to cure him, to which his wife responds by wondering why newspapers give the age of the deceased but never that of the newly born. Name this Absurdist play, the first by Eugene Ionesco.

This man's most famous work begins by stating that the blood of "Papists and Protestants" is not required by Jesus Christ and then presents a dialogue between personifications of Truth and Peace. This author of A Key to the Language of America and The Bloudy Tenant of Persecution was closely associated with the Narragansett tribe, and his dispute with the founder of the Quakers led to the work George Fox Digg'd Out of His Burrowes. Known for his feud with John Cotton, name this man banished from Plymouth colony in 1635, the eventual founder of Rhode Island.

This poem's hero, whose "eyes but close / To look within," travels to a Hall of Arimanes. He tells a pretty witch "Though it torture me, ‘tis but the same / My pang shall find a voice." Remarking that he needs "no further guidance," he attempts to send away a "chamois hunter." A written charm gives him power over spirits, the seventh of which comments "Nor to slumber, nor to die / Shall be in thy destiny." name this semi- autobiographical poem set "amongst the Higher Alps", whose morbid titular hero seeks his own demise after the death of his beloved Astarte, written by Lord Byron.

This man, the owner of Animus Consulting, scored the first basket made in Miami's American Airlines Arena while playing for the Orlando Magic. His college career began at Vanderbilt, but he transferred in 1994, becoming the fourth-leading career rebounder at Penn State. He spent the 2001 through 2003 seasons as backup center for the Utah Jazz, whose owner apparently wouldn't allow Brokeback Mountain to be shown in his movie theaters. Name this author of Man in the Middle and enemy of Tim Hardaway, who recently became the first NBA player to come out of the closet.

The novels A Wreath for Udomo and Mine Boy are set in this nation, as is a drama concerning the waiters Sam and Willie and novels about the communications professor David Lurie and a gardener named Michael. In another work set here, Julie Summers' car breaks down and Abdu works as an auto mechanic, while in yet another novel, the Smales family is rescued by their servant July. Name this country featuring such authors as Peter Abrahams, J.M. Coetzee, Athol Fugard, and Nadine Gordimer.

His career began with a 1935 work about the Berger family in which the patriarch, Jacob, kills himself to leave money to his grandson Ralph. His screenplay for the 1936 bomb The General Died at Dawn prompted critic Frank Nugent to make a pun using his name followed by "where is thy sting?" This man, the basis of the character Barton Fink, created a movie star named Charlie Castle and satirized Hollywood in The Big Knife, and also createda violinist-turned-boxer named Joe Bonaparte in Golden Boy. Name this American playwright who wrote about a cabdrivers' strike in Waiting for Lefty.

This work's second section ends with an invocation to "let everyone fly out of Sodom" and argues that its addresses have an "extraordinary opportunity" because "the door of mercy [has been thrown] wide open." Based on a verse from the twenty-third chapter of Deuteronomy, "Their foot shall slide in due time," its first part mentions "wicked men" kept out of Hell by God's pleasure, although the speaker constantly warns that God's wrath will send all the subjects there, likening them to a spider held over a fire. Name this 1741 sermon by Jonathan Edwards.
Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God
